rationale: Proverbs aims to give perception to the innocent and the young; the psalm says the disclosure of God's words gives understanding to the simple. Both describe instruction benefiting inexperienced hearers.
Wisdom describes repeatedly calling without obedience; Isaiah's judgment likewise answers the failure to obey when the Lord called and the disregard shown when He spoke.
Applying the ear to wisdom and the heart to understanding is echoed by the commands to apply the ear to the father's words and keep them in the heart.
Seeking wisdom as silver and hidden treasure is complemented by the later valuation of trading in wisdom above treasures of gold and silver.
The Lord shields the journey of those acting rightly; the psalm combines God's blameless way with His being a protector of all who hope in Him.
Delight and rejoicing in evil correspond to the fool doing evil things in laughter in chapter 10; both portray wrongdoing as a source of pleasure to the fool.
The removal of ungodly and lawless people from the land corresponds to the psalm's destruction of evildoers and inheritance of the land by those waiting for the Lord.

Mercy and faithfulness are to be fastened around the neck here; the later instruction collars parental laws around the neck and fastens them upon the soul. Both make moral instruction a personal adornment.
Wealth and glory in Wisdom's left hand correspond to her later declaration that wealth and glory belong to her alongside righteous possession.
Wisdom carries law and mercy on her tongue; the final portrait joins a woman's wise, lawful speech with mercy that raises up her children. Both connect wisdom's speech with law and merciful conduct.
Fearless sitting and pleasant sleep correspond to the psalmist lying down and sleeping in peace because the Lord makes him dwell in hope.
Freedom from approaching fright and ungodly assaults is paired with the righteous person's lack of fear at an evil report and established heart while facing enemies.
The Lord's support of the foot so it is not shaken corresponds to the prayer against a shaking foot and the assurance of the wakeful Lord as keeper and shelter.
Honoring Wisdom brings exaltation and her embrace here; Sirach describes Wisdom raising her sons high and promising inherited glory to the person holding her fast.
Applying the ear to the father's words repeats the earlier direction that the ear obey wisdom and the heart attend to understanding.

Proverbs urges guarding the heart as the source of life's outlets; Jesus locates evil reasonings and deeds coming from within the heart and defiling the person. Both assign consequential outward expression to the inner heart.
